case_name: Ishar Singh v District and Sessions Judge and Another
respondent:
District and Sessions Judge and Another
Supreme Court of India

11 February 1999
S.L.P. (C) No. 2906 of 1998 (From the Judgment and Order Dt. 22 December 1997 of the Punjab and Haryana High Court in C.W.P. No. 18290 of 1997)
The Judgment was delivered by: D. P. WADHWA, J.
1.  This petition is directed against the order dated 22-12-1997 of the Punjab and Haryana High Court dismissing the writ petition filed by the petitioner seeking quashing of the orders of the authorities for taking possession of public premises under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971 (for short "the PP Act"). The lease of the public premises had been resumed under the provisions of the Capital of Punjab (Development and Regulation) Act, 1952 and the Chandigarh Lease-hold of Sites and Buildings Rules, 1973 (for short "the Act" and "the Rules"). The public premises comprise a booth/shop for the trade of furniture bearing No. 225, Sector 34-D, Chandigarh.
2.  By letter date
facts: The lease of the public premises had been resumed under the provisions of the Capital of Punjab (Development and Regulation) Act, 1952 and the Chandigarh Lease-hold of Sites and Buildings Rules, 1973.

By letter dated 3-9-1979, the booth was allotted on lease to Niranjan Kaur and her four sons Ishar Singh, Pritpal Singh, Bablu and Bintu (@ Inderjit Singh and Sardul Singh) by the Estate Officer, Chandigarh Administration.
The public premises comprise a booth/shop for the trade of furniture bearing No. 225, Sector 34-D, Chandigarh.
Possession of the allottees or anyone claiming through them of the booth thus became unauthorised.
Proceedings were held under the PP Act for taking physical possession of the booth.
Against this order of the Estate Officer, an appeal was filed by Ishar Singh, one of the original allottees, to the District Judge under Section 9 of the PP Act.
issues: Whether proper opportunity had been given to the appellants before the order under Section 5 of the PP Act was made by the Estate Officer.
Whether the notices under the PP Act were properly served on the original allottees.
petitioner_arguments: The contention of the allottees that a partnership had been entered into between M/s Kang Enterprises was repelled.
Ishar Singh, one of the original allottees, filed an appeal before the District Judge, Chandigarh under Section 9 of the PP Act.
Ishar Singh then filed a petition in the High Court invoking its jurisdiction under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution.
respondent_arguments: The Estate Officer had issued an authority letter on 21-12-1997 for eviction of all the unauthorised occupants of the booth and that in execution of the eviction warrants the premises were sealed on 24-1-1998 by Mr Prem Chand, Sub-Inspector (Enforcement) from the Office of the Estate Officer, Chandigarh.
court_reasoning: The District Judge wondered how Ishar Singh came to know about the order dated 16-5-1996 on 2-2-1997.
He did not find any ground for condoning the delay in filing the appeal by Ishar Singh and dismissed the same as barred by time by order dated 13-11-1997.
The Estate Officer has stated that this 'Shri Akhand Path' was kept by Bhag Singh in order to defeat the legal action to take possession of the booth being the public premises.
holding: There is no merit in this petition. It is dismissed with costs.
